By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Paid

Summary:
Own Goal – Shawn Mkhize and the Royal AM Football Club.


Msunduzi or Pietermaritzburg is like many municipalities in South Africa, bankrupt and under administration because of poor budget control and lack of essential services.

https://www.news24.com/news24/politics/confidential-report-shows-treasurys-scathing-review-of-collapsing-anc-led-msunduzi-municipality-20230928

A confidential government report has revealed how National Treasury delivered a scathing review of the governance and financial health at the ANC-led Msunduzi Local Municipality in KwaZulu-Natal.
The report – authored by Treasury's Kgomotso Baloyi – says the municipality's service delivery and financial health are "in decline" and its institutional arrangements "fragile".

Msunduzi
Krishnan said in her presentation that Msunduzi had been found to be in a poor state with “dysfunctional” ward committees, public protests, a bank overdraft and the treasury having taken the decision to stop payments to the municipality when the provincial government intervened.
“There was a failure by the council to resolve service delivery challenges [waste management, roads management and electricity] and there was underspending and under budgeting,” Krishnan said.
As a result of the lack of maintenance of infrastructure, the municipality had faced frequent electricity outages. It had failed to hold councillors accountable for absenteeism, to exercise oversight on management and on conditional grants and to investigate allegations of malfeasance and maladministration against senior managers and leaders of the municipality.
The municipality received an adverse audit opinion from the auditor general for the 2017-18 financial year, which it had improved to a qualified audit opinion in 2018-19. But it still had poor financial management and failed to prevent and investigate unauthorised, irregular, fruitless and wasteful expenditure of more than R361.22 million.
It had also failed to institute consequence management measures for managers and other officials responsible for the failure to obtain authority to designate eight office bearers as full-time councillors.
Krishnan said the cooperative governance department had filed a section 106 forensic investigation report with 17 recommendations that the municipality had tabled in 2020. Fifteen of these recommendations had been implemented and two were in progress. A further section 106 report with 27 recommendations was tabled in 2021, but only four of these had been implemented.
“The municipality regressed to a qualified audit opinion. Poor financial management
persisted although the overdraft was paid off and cash coverage improved slightly,” Krishnan said.
She said the municipality still owed its creditors R126.5 million excluding arrearsof R395.6 million and R515.9 million it owes Eskom and Umgeni Water respectively. Its current Eskom debt is R199.9 million.
After the intervention, 98% of the municipality’s wards are, in 2023, now functional and the council has “fairly resolved” service delivery related issues, while spending 7% of its budget on operations and maintenance.
“We are seeing an improvement and in the next six to eight months Msunduzi will be able to exit the intervention,” Krishnan said.

Faced with such an extremely dire financial situation what remedy do you think the Msunduzi powers that be have decided to spend their money on?

27 million over 3 years for Shawn Mhkize’s Royal AM Football Club.
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_AM_F.C.
(What is it with powerful women and soccer clubs?)

Shawn Mhkize is possibly one of the wealthiest women in South Africa. Previously married to S’bu Mpisane they were known as Durban’s Teflon couple.

CONVICTED fraudster Shauwn Mpisane has been awarded government tenders worth more than R1.1-billion in the past seven years, despite fighting off a series of fraud charges and criminal investigations.
Details of the Durban contractor's wealth and "frustrating" investigations by the taxman and National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) into her lucrative business dealings have been laid bare in papers before the High Court in Pietermaritzburg.
Mpisane, 37, who has amassed a multimillion-rand fortune from building low-cost government houses, is facing fresh charges of fraud after being accused of submitting forged documents to obtain Construction Industry Development Board gradings, which were used to win government tenders worth R140-million.
Court papers detail some of the tenders awarded to her company between 2005 and last year. They include:
• A R482-million tender awarded by the eThekwini municipality in August last year to build 2825 low-cost houses in Umlazi, north of Durban;
• A R176-million contract awarded by the municipality in KwaDukuza, north of Durban, to build 1980 houses;
• A R13.9-million contract to refurbish Truro House, a building that accommodates the provincial department of education's offices in Durban;
• A R26.9-million contract awarded by the KwaZulu-Natal department of public works for the building of Molweni Primary School outside Durban; and
• A R21-million tender, also awarded by the provincial department of public works, to build a clinic in Inanda, north of Durban.
These major projects, as well as other, smaller tenders, bring the worth of projects awarded to her company in the past seven years to more than R1.1-billion.
In her affidavit this week, Mpisane said: "I have every intention to clear my name and to prove in the criminal proceedings that there is no basis for the allegations against me."
For almost a decade her company, Zikhulise Cleaning, Maintenance and Transport, has been the subject of several fraud and forensic investigations into alleged tender irregularities. In the court papers she described how the investigations were affecting her family and business.
"I am constantly incurring legal costs amounting to millions of rands. My family is being humiliated. I am not able to focus on my business because of this harassment by the national director of public prosecutions ... and all state organs that have the power to charge and frustrate my business are doing so all the time."
Last week, members of the NPA's Asset Forfeiture Unit, escorted by anti-corruption task team agents, swooped on her R25-million mansion in La Lucia, north of Durban, with an order to seize assets worth R140-million.
A fleet of 60 cars, worth more than R30-million, was attached.
Among the cars was a Rolls-Royce Phantom estimated to cost R6-million, a Ferrari 612 Scaglietti valued at more than R3-million, and a Rolls-Royce Ghost estimated to cost R4.8-million.
Social media
In 2020 she started to use social media and in eight months she gained over 1 million followers on Instagram.[13] Since then her fans and followers have given her the title of "mother of the nation".[14] In October 2020, she was nominated for Socialite of the Year and Fag Hag of the Year at the Feather Awards.[15]
Personal life
Shauwn Mkhize was married to Sbu Mpisane; they divorced in 2019. They had one son. Sbu Mpisane already had a daughter.[16]
Controversies
Mkhize has been convicted of fraud and in 2013 owed the South African Revenue Service over R200 million.[17][18]

Back to the soccer club.
Royal AM (also known as "Thwihli Thwahla") is a South African football club based in Durban, KwaZulu Natal that plays in the DSTV Premiership.
History
In 2019, Shauwn Mkhize and her son Andile Mpisane purchased Real Kings, renaming it Royal AM.[2]
They bought their right to play in the top tier after purchasing the Premiership license from Bloemfontein Celtic in August 2021.[3][4]
The club received a transfer ban from FIFA effective 3 July 2023 after unlawfully terminating the contract of Samir Nurkovic and failing to pay the outstanding amount of R12 million.[5]
Already in history books
In that time, Thwihli Thwahla has since entered the world record books. IOL reported that Royal has used the second-most players on the planet in the last five years. This was according to a study conducted by the CIES Football Observatory, which researched 75 of the biggest leagues on the planet.
The Durban-based club has used a whopping 166 players in just four years, second behind Brazilian club AA Ponte Preta, with 168 players. By the study's definition, this makes Royal the 'second most unstable club on the planet'.

Msunduzi Municipality: Own Goal

1 V/O
This is the story of a collapsing municipality…

Mel
It has been run badly for a couple of years and now the chickens are coming home to roost.

2 V/O
A mayor of a provincial capital - who seems to be in denial…

Executive Mayor: Mzimkhulu Thebolla
This municipality is now back on the road to its functionality.

3 V/O
A soccer team owned by a reality TV star, tenderpreneur and convicted fraudster…

Mkhize
When God shows up for me he shows off!

4 V/O
Her son, who was the first teenage chairman - and sometimes captain - of the PSL team his mother bought him.

Andile
My name is Andile Mpisane, the new chairman of Royal AM.

5 V/O
And the disturbing question of a R27 million rand sponsorship deal.
Fade to black / Fade up

6 V/O
Pietermaritzburg, with its wealth of Victorian heritage, can seem like a city where time has slowed down.
Like many inner cities in the country, service delivery is noticeably lacking. The roads are pockmarked with potholes, litter collects unchecked… diming traffic lights stand as reminders of a forgotten order.

Kantha
The decay/collapse of the city is causing a lot of frustration. Just exiting our store you would see the congestion of taxis and the traffic disorder.




7 V/O
For over a hundred years, the clothing store Asmalls has been dressing the city's residents, but business is becoming challenging. Kantha Naidoo, who's been with the company for 17 years, gives us a firsthand look at the issues they face every day.

Kantha
The wall has become a urinal and as you can see the drainage system so we have to get this cleaned up regularly. So as a result of the wall becoming a urinal. We have put in a sprinkler system and we have created our own concept. The water will come through and flush out and we get somebody to come through and clean pavement with sheep dip etc.

Govan
It smells terrible.

Kantha
It does but this is a good day.

8 V/O
Kantha Naidoo says while the municipality does clean the main streets, the side streets are ignored and have turned into dumping sites.
To take charge, businesses rent a skip and hire workers to sanitise the gutters and remove the garbage.

To address the urine problem, they “innovated”.

Govan link
This is what it has come to in the Pietermaritzburg City centre, the stench here …

9 V/O
It’s almost suffocating.

Govan link
…the stench here is overwhelming. This urinal was installed by the businesses who can’t count on the city to clean up drain the answers or even truck away the waste.

10 V/O
Pietermaritzburg is run by the Msunduzi Municipality, which was placed under administration in 2019 for a host of problems - including irregular expenditure, maladministration…and councillor absenteeism.

The Pietermaritzburg & Midlands Chamber of Commerce, speaks for about 700 business owners who worry about the city's future. Melanie Veness heads it up.

Govan
So Melanie, how would you describe the business sentiment in the Msunduzi Municipality right now?

Mel
Desperate. Absolutely desperate.
From a service delivery point of view our companies are really battling. It’s gotten so bad for some businesses, the insecurity and the poor quality of electricity supply that some big manufacturers have threatened to stop using Pietermaritzburg companies.

V/O 11
When it was placed under administration in 2019 Msunduzi owed Eskom 209 million rands, nearly five years later and they now owe 881 million rands. And a further 521 million rands to uMngeni-uThukela water… cash flow has been dire for years.

Mel
“We are probably around 20 days, it’s definitely less than one month.”

Govan
“Less than a month’s money. That is dangerous territory.”

Mel
Ja we are in very dangerous waters

UPS Soccer Whistle

12 V/O
Despite its staggering … and spiralling debts, Executive Mayor Mzimkhulu Thebolla recently proudly announced that Msunduzi would be sponsoring a soccer team to the tune of 27 million rands over the next three years.

Govan
Tell me, Mr. Mayor, why did the municipality decide to sponsor the Royal AM Football Club?

Mayor
Look this is a very old story now. When Council took that decision we knew there was no direct benefit to the municipality I mean in terms of rands and cents that would be paid into the city’s coffers.

Govan
Then you are convinced it is a benefit, even if it's not rands and cents.

Mayor
I am convinced and I believe that the people of the city are convinced.



13 V/O
This is the Royal Ranch or the training grounds of the club that is on the receiving end of money from a struggling municipality

So who are they?

Well, none other than nouveau riche sensation - a football club called Royal AM
… owned by flamboyant reality TV star and convicted fraudster Shauwn Mkhize.

Worth hundreds of millions of rands Shauwn Mkhize lives a lavish lifestyle, having accumulated her wealth through government tenders worth over a billion rands for affordable housing around Durban.

Despite facing well-publicized fraud convictions and allegations of tax avoidance by SARS, she flaunts her success.

ADD UPSOUNDS HERE


Link
Shauwn Mkhize says she started a football club for her son and then named it Royal AM. Or is it Royal Andile Mpisane. Either way, since then, she's made millions in sponsorships from municipalities.

14 V/O
When Andile Mpisane was just 19, his dream of playing in the Premier Soccer League came true… because his mother bought him his very own team… the PSL rights for the Royal AM team cost her a mere 50 million rand.

Andile Mkhize
At the moment. I'm the chairman of the club and I've announced Mam’ Mkhize to be president.

SM
I've never thought that one day my son, you know, that I've carried for nine months, will appoint me as a president.

15 V/O
Like mother, like son, Andile Mpisane lives by the mantra, 'If you've got it, flaunt it.'
Not only is he the chairman of his own club now, but he plays and captains as he pleases.
Soccer pundits have criticized him for playing when many believe he lacks the talent or stamina.

Metro FM
Andile Ncube
And I can imagine the critique that comes with it. Does that bother you at all?

Shauwn
So it doesn’t matter what they say, he must just focus on what he wants to do and I will support him.

Link
Shauwn Mkhize is probably the most controversial soccer boss in South Africa but she is also not very good at it. Royal AM has had 166 players in 5 years that makes them the second worst managed club in the world.

16 V/O
They’ve been fined hundreds of thousands of rands by soccer authorities for infringements - like this one, where Shauwn Mkhize brazenly handed out wads of cash to her players on the pitch in front of television cameras, immediately after winning a match.

When we approached Royal AM for an interview, they declined, citing the sensitivity of the matter.

Govan
Weren’t you cautious or concerned that the reputation of the team might sully the reputation of the municipality.

Mayor
For us, we must have a team that participates in the elite league. That was what was important for us as to who are the personalities behind the team, what are they doing, provided they comply with the laws of this country, then we have a partner.

Link
Included in the sponsorship deal is the upkeep of the Harry Gwala Stadium by the municipality for an unspecified amount.

Mel
And we were and remain horrified that we would basically have our council going to approve a blank check because whatever happens at that stadium can be put down to maintenance and another municipality must pay that some money that must go to.

17 V/O
The DA opposition in the council has taken the sponsorship matter to court because they say it was never budgeted for - they want the money to be paid back and used for service delivery.

18 V/O
The Mayor though isn’t budging.

Mayor
Out of sponsoring that team business thrives in the city. I know in the next two weeks Kaizer Chiefs will be playing in the city. For that whole week everybody from everywhere are in the city.

19 V/O
Businesses can’t see what benefit a soccer sponsorship will bring.

Kantha
It is quite frustrating to hear that our monies are being used for a football club. As business that’s not in the priority list, contribute so that us who are contributing to the rates base can thrive.

20 V/O
But the Mayor is confident that his tenure will see the municipality exit administration and become fully functional.

Mayor
I am actually very proud now to stand up everywhere and say that I am the mayor of the city to because of the achievements we are making.

Govan
Mr Mayor the businesses in the city don’t agree; they believe that things are getting worse?
And the question that is arising is how can you justify the sponsorship of a football club?

Mayor
No, for this financial year alone our annual budget is sitting at 8.6 billion. So, now we only sponsor a soccer team, by R 9 million per annum.

Govan
Not including tax and you pay for the upkeep

Mayor
Including all the costs.

And you pay for the stadium?

Mayor
Including all the costs.

Govan
It’s 27 million not including the value added tax. Or the CPI inflation. And you are paying for upkeep of Harry Gwala Stadium

Mayor
Yes, because we also don’t want it to be a white elephant that is a 2010 Legacy Stadium.

Govan
It does make sense

Mayor
If nobody utilises that facility then it says 78 million spent to build that iconic stadium went to waste.

21 V/O
In the end this is a story about a city in decline - with a stagnant economy - that will be giving money to a millionaire soccer boss for the three years, while investors and residents suffer from a lack of leadership and its obvious consequences.


Promos

Promo 1

Pietermaritzburg's Msunduzi Municipality is drowning in over one billion Rands worth of utility debts, yet they're splurging tens of millions on soccer sponsorship.

Mayor
For us, we must have a team that participates in the elite league.


Promo 2

The newest team on the block owned by the youngest PSL chairman, has just secured sponsorship, from a municipality that can’t meet it’s debts or stop the decay.

Mel
Desperate. Absolutely desperate.

Govan
“Less than a month’s money. That is dangerous territory.”

Mel
Ja we are in very dangerous waters


Promo 3
A flamboyant millionaire buys her son his very own PSL soccer team and names it after him. They just scored a sponsorship from a municipality drowning in debt and decay.

Shauwn
When God shows up for me he shows off!

OR
Govan
Then you are convinced it is a benefit, even if it's not rands and cents.

Mayor
I am convinced and I believe that the people of the city are convinced.




Another optional end statement from Kantha

Kantha
I mean, I can see us leaving, but we are invested in the city. I mean, this is a family run business. We can’t just pack up and go. We have employees that are dependent on us. They have mouths to feed so we can't say we're going to pack up and leave. We'd be affecting the economy of the city..

collapsing municipality… Mel It has been run badly for a couple of years and now the chickens are coming home to roost. 2 V/O A mayor of a provincial capital - who seems to be in denial… Executive Mayor: Mzimkhulu Thebolla This municipality is now back on the road to its functionality. 3 V/O A soccer team owned by a reality TV star, tenderpreneur and convicted fraudster… Mkhize When God shows up for me he shows off! 4 V/O Her son, who was the first teenage chairman - and sometimes captain - of the PSL team his mother bought him. Andile My name is Andile Mpisane, the new chairman of Royal AM. 5 V/O And the disturbing question of a R27 million rand sponsorship deal. Fade to black / Fade up 6 V/O Pietermaritzburg, with its wealth of Victorian heritage, can seem like a city where time has slowed down. Like many inner cities in the country, service delivery is noticeably lacking. The roads are pockmarked with potholes, litter collects unchecked… diming traffic lights stand as reminders of a forgotten order. Kantha The decay/collapse of the city is causing a lot of frustration. Just exiting our store you would see the congestion of taxis and the traffic disorder. 7 V/O For over a hundred years, the clothing store Asmalls has been dressing the city's residents, but business is becoming challenging. Kantha Naidoo, who's been with the company for 17 years, gives us a firsthand look at the issues they face every day. Kantha The wall has become a urinal and as you can see the drainage system so we have to get this cleaned up regularly. So as a result of the wall becoming a urinal. We have put in a sprinkler system and we have created our own concept. The water will come through and flush out and we get somebody to come through and clean pavement with sheep dip etc. Govan It smells terrible. Kantha It does but this is a good day. 8 V/O Kantha Naidoo says while the municipality does clean the main streets, the side streets are ignored and have turned into dumping sites. To take charge, businesses rent a skip and hire workers to sanitise the gutters and remove the garbage. To address the urine problem, they “innovated”. Govan link This is what it has come to in the Pietermaritzburg City centre, the stench here … 9 V/O It’s almost suffocating. Govan link …the stench here is overwhelming. This urinal was installed by the businesses who can’t count on the city to clean up drain the answers or even truck away the waste. 10 V/O Pietermaritzburg is run by the Msunduzi Municipality, which was placed under administration in 2019 for a host of problems - including irregular expenditure, maladministration…and councillor absenteeism. The Pietermaritzburg & Midlands Chamber of Commerce, speaks for about 700 business owners who worry about the city's future. Melanie Veness heads it up. Govan So Melanie, how would you describe the business sentiment in the Msunduzi Municipality right now? Mel Desperate. Absolutely desperate. From a service delivery point of view our companies are really battling. It’s gotten so bad for some businesses, the insecurity and the poor quality of electricity supply that some big manufacturers have threatened to stop using Pietermaritzburg companies. V/O 11 When it was placed under administration in 2019 Msunduzi owed Eskom 209 million rands, nearly five years later and they now owe 881 million rands. And a further 521 million rands to uMngeni-uThukela water… cash flow has been dire for years. Mel “We are probably around 20 days, it’s definitely less than one month.” Govan “Less than a month’s money. That is dangerous territory.” Mel Ja we are in very dangerous waters UPS Soccer Whistle 12 V/O Despite its staggering … and spiralling debts, Executive Mayor Mzimkhulu Thebolla recently proudly announced that Msunduzi would be sponsoring a soccer team to the tune of 27 million rands over the next three years. Govan Tell me, Mr. Mayor, why did the municipality decide to sponsor the Royal AM Football Club? Mayor Look this is a very old story now. When Council took that decision we knew there was no direct benefit to the municipality I mean in terms of rands and cents that would be paid into the city’s coffers. Govan Then you are convinced it is a benefit, even if it's not rands and cents. Mayor I am convinced and I believe that the people of the city are convinced. 13 V/O This is the Royal Ranch or the training grounds of the club that is on the receiving end of money from a struggling municipality So who are they? Well, none other than nouveau riche sensation - a football club called Royal AM … owned by flamboyant reality TV star and convicted fraudster Shauwn Mkhize. Worth hundreds of millions of rands Shauwn Mkhize lives a lavish lifestyle, having accumulated her wealth through government tenders worth over a billion rands for affordable housing around Durban. Despite facing well-publicized fraud convictions and allegations of tax avoidance by SARS, she flaunts her success. ADD UPSOUNDS HERE Link Shauwn Mkhize says she started a football club for her son and then named it Royal AM. Or is it Royal Andile Mpisane. Either way, since then, she's made millions in sponsorships from municipalities. 14 V/O When Andile Mpisane was just 19, his dream of playing in the Premier Soccer League came true… because his mother bought him his very own team… the PSL rights for the Royal AM team cost her a mere 50 million rand. Andile Mkhize At the moment. I'm the chairman of the club and I've announced Mam’ Mkhize to be president. SM I've never thought that one day my son, you know, that I've carried for nine months, will appoint me as a president. 15 V/O Like mother, like son, Andile Mpisane lives by the mantra, 'If you've got it, flaunt it.' Not only is he the chairman of his own club now, but he plays and captains as he pleases. Soccer pundits have criticized him for playing when many believe he lacks the talent or stamina. Metro FM Andile Ncube And I can imagine the critique that comes with it. Does that bother you at all? Shauwn So it doesn’t matter what they say, he must just focus on what he wants to do and I will support him. Link Shauwn Mkhize is probably the most controversial soccer boss in South Africa but she is also not very good at it. Royal AM has had 166 players in 5 years that makes them the second worst managed club in the world. 16 V/O They’ve been fined hundreds of thousands of rands by soccer authorities for infringements - like this one, where Shauwn Mkhize brazenly handed out wads of cash to her players on the pitch in front of television cameras, immediately after winning a match. When we approached Royal AM for an interview, they declined, citing the sensitivity of the matter. Govan Weren’t you cautious or concerned that the reputation of the team might sully the reputation of the municipality. Mayor For us, we must have a team that participates in the elite league. That was what was important for us as to who are the personalities behind the team, what are they doing, provided they comply with the laws of this country, then we have a partner. Link Included in the sponsorship deal is the upkeep of the Harry Gwala Stadium by the municipality for an unspecified amount. Mel And we were and remain horrified that we would basically have our council going to approve a blank check because whatever happens at that stadium can be put down to maintenance and another municipality must pay that some money that must go to. 17 V/O The DA opposition in the council has taken the sponsorship matter to court because they say it was never budgeted for - they want the money to be paid back and used for service delivery. 18 V/O The Mayor though isn’t budging. Mayor Out of sponsoring that team business thrives in the city. I know in the next two weeks Kaizer Chiefs will be playing in the city. For that whole week everybody from everywhere are in the city. 19 V/O Businesses can’t see what benefit a soccer sponsorship will bring. Kantha It is quite frustrating to hear that our monies are being used for a football club. As business that’s not in the priority list, contribute so that us who are contributing to the rates base can thrive. 20 V/O But the Mayor is confident that his tenure will see the municipality exit administration and become fully functional. Mayor I am actually very proud now to stand up everywhere and say that I am the mayor of the city to because of the achievements we are making. Govan Mr Mayor the businesses in the city don’t agree; they believe that things are getting worse? And the question that is arising is how can you justify the sponsorship of a football club? Mayor No, for this financial year alone our annual budget is sitting at 8.6 billion. So, now we only sponsor a soccer team, by R 9 million per annum. Govan Not including tax and you pay for the upkeep Mayor Including all the costs. And you pay for the stadium? Mayor Including all the costs. Govan It’s 27 million not including the value added tax. Or the CPI inflation. And you are paying for upkeep of Harry Gwala Stadium Mayor Yes, because we also don’t want it to be a white elephant that is a 2010 Legacy Stadium. Govan It does make sense Mayor If nobody utilises that facility then it says 78 million spent to build that iconic stadium went to waste. 21 V/O In the end this is a story about a city in decline - with a stagnant economy - that will be giving money to a millionaire soccer boss for the three years, while investors and residents suffer from a lack of leadership and its obvious consequences. Msunduzi or Pietermaritzburg is like many municipalities in South Africa, bankrupt and under administration because of poor budget control and lack of essential services. https://www.news24.com/news24/politics/confidential-report-shows-treasurys-scathing-review-of-collapsing-anc-led-msunduzi-municipality-20230928 A confidential government report has revealed how National Treasury delivered a scathing review of the governance and financial health at the ANC-led Msunduzi Local Municipality in KwaZulu-Natal. The report – authored by Treasury's Kgomotso Baloyi – says the municipality's service delivery and financial health are "in decline" and its institutional arrangements "fragile". Msunduzi Krishnan said in her presentation that Msunduzi had been found to be in a poor state with “dysfunctional” ward committees, public protests, a bank overdraft and the treasury having taken the decision to stop payments to the municipality when the provincial government intervened. “There was a failure by the council to resolve service delivery challenges [waste management, roads management and electricity] and there was underspending and under budgeting,” Krishnan said. As a result of the lack of maintenance of infrastructure, the municipality had faced frequent electricity outages. It had failed to hold councillors accountable for absenteeism, to exercise oversight on management and on conditional grants and to investigate allegations of malfeasance and maladministration against senior managers and leaders of the municipality. The municipality received an adverse audit opinion from the auditor general for the 2017-18 financial year, which it had improved to a qualified audit opinion in 2018-19. But it still had poor financial management and failed to prevent and investigate unauthorised, irregular, fruitless and wasteful expenditure of more than R361.22 million. It had also failed to institute consequence management measures for managers and other officials responsible for the failure to obtain authority to designate eight office bearers as full-time councillors. Krishnan said the cooperative governance department had filed a section 106 forensic investigation report with 17 recommendations that the municipality had tabled in 2020. Fifteen of these recommendations had been implemented and two were in progress. A further section 106 report with 27 recommendations was tabled in 2021, but only four of these had been implemented. “The municipality regressed to a qualified audit opinion. Poor financial management persisted although the overdraft was paid off and cash coverage improved slightly,” Krishnan said. She said the municipality still owed its creditors R126.5 million excluding arrearsof R395.6 million and R515.9 million it owes Eskom and Umgeni Water respectively. Its current Eskom debt is R199.9 million. After the intervention, 98% of the municipality’s wards are, in 2023, now functional and the council has “fairly resolved” service delivery related issues, while spending 7% of its budget on operations and maintenance. “We are seeing an improvement and in the next six to eight months Msunduzi will be able to exit the intervention,” Krishnan said. Faced with such an extremely dire financial situation what remedy do you think the Msunduzi powers that be have decided to spend their money on? 27 million over 3 years for Shawn Mhkize’s Royal AM Football Club. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Royal_AM_F.C. (What is it with powerful women and soccer clubs?) Shawn Mhkize is possibly one of the wealthiest women in South Africa. Previously married to S’bu Mpisane they were known as Durban’s Teflon couple. CONVICTED fraudster Shauwn Mpisane has been awarded government tenders worth more than R1.1-billion in the past seven years, despite fighting off a series of fraud charges and criminal investigations. Details of the Durban contractor's wealth and "frustrating" investigations by the taxman and National Prosecuting Authority (NPA) into her lucrative business dealings have been laid bare in papers before the High Court in Pietermaritzburg. Mpisane, 37, who has amassed a multimillion-rand fortune from building low-cost government houses, is facing fresh charges of fraud after being accused of submitting forged documents to obtain Construction Industry Development Board gradings, which were used to win government tenders worth R140-million. Court papers detail some of the tenders awarded to her company between 2005 and last year. They include: • A R482-million tender awarded by the eThekwini municipality in August last year to build 2825 low-cost houses in Umlazi, north of Durban; • A R176-million contract awarded by the municipality in KwaDukuza, north of Durban, to build 1980 houses; • A R13.9-million contract to refurbish Truro House, a building that accommodates the provincial department of education's offices in Durban; • A R26.9-million contract awarded by the KwaZulu-Natal department of public works for the building of Molweni Primary School outside Durban; and • A R21-million tender, also awarded by the provincial department of public works, to build a clinic in Inanda, north of Durban. These major projects, as well as other, smaller tenders, bring the worth of projects awarded to her company in the past seven years to more than R1.1-billion. In her affidavit this week, Mpisane said: "I have every intention to clear my name and to prove in the criminal proceedings that there is no basis for the allegations against me." For almost a decade her company, Zikhulise Cleaning, Maintenance and Transport, has been the subject of several fraud and forensic investigations into alleged tender irregularities. In the court papers she described how the investigations were affecting her family and business. "I am constantly incurring legal costs amounting to millions of rands. My family is being humiliated. I am not able to focus on my business because of this harassment by the national director of public prosecutions ... and all state organs that have the power to charge and frustrate my business are doing so all the time." Last week, members of the NPA's Asset Forfeiture Unit, escorted by anti-corruption task team agents, swooped on her R25-million mansion in La Lucia, north of Durban, with an order to seize assets worth R140-million. A fleet of 60 cars, worth more than R30-million, was attached. Among the cars was a Rolls-Royce Phantom estimated to cost R6-million, a Ferrari 612 Scaglietti valued at more than R3-million, and a Rolls-Royce Ghost estimated to cost R4.8-million. Social media In 2020 she started to use social media and in eight months she gained over 1 million followers on Instagram.[13] Since then her fans and followers have given her the title of "mother of the nation".[14] In October 2020, she was nominated for Socialite of the Year and Fag Hag of the Year at the Feather Awards.[15] Personal life Shauwn Mkhize was married to Sbu Mpisane; they divorced in 2019. They had one son. Sbu Mpisane already had a daughter.[16] Controversies Mkhize has been convicted of fraud and in 2013 owed the South African Revenue Service over R200 million.[17][18] Awards and nominations Year Award Category Result 2020 Feather Awards Socialite of the Year Nominated[19] Fag Hag of the Year Nominated[19] Hollywood and African Prestigious Awards Women of the Year Won[20] Best Reality TV Show Won[21] 2022 2022 DStv Mzansi Viewers' Choice Awards Favourite personality Nominated[22] Back to the soccer club. Royal AM (also known as "Thwihli Thwahla") is a South African football club based in Durban, KwaZulu Natal that plays in the DSTV Premiership. History In 2019, Shauwn Mkhize and her son Andile Mpisane purchased Real Kings, renaming it Royal AM.[2] They bought their right to play in the top tier after purchasing the Premiership license from Bloemfontein Celtic in August 2021.[3][4] The club received a transfer ban from FIFA effective 3 July 2023 after unlawfully terminating the contract of Samir Nurkovic and failing to pay the outstanding amount of R12 million.[5] Already in history books In that time, Thwihli Thwahla has since entered the world record books. IOL reported that Royal has used the second-most players on the planet in the last five years. This was according to a study conducted by the CIES Football Observatory, which researched 75 of the biggest leagues on the planet. The Durban-based club has used a whopping 166 players in just four years, second behind Brazilian club AA Ponte Preta, with 168 players. By the study's definition, this makes Royal the 'second most unstable club on the planet'.
